oliver: quick thread on slot fragmentation + a small mitigation prototype i ran on staging. saw p99 tail jump during mixed tiny/long workload.
zara: saw that too. which metric looked most telling?
oliver: two things: high free_slot_count with low batch_fill_ratio and a spike in eviction_events for tiny requests.
noah: so gaps + reactive eviction. did you try padding?
oliver: yeah i added a "pad pool" per GPU (4KB equivalent ~= 32 tokens) that accepts tiny requests best-effort. results: p99 down ~18% but overall throughput dip ~2%.
grace: interesting. pad pool seems promising. how does it interact with kv-cache affinity?
oliver: we kept pad requests separate; they never bind to long-context kv pages. pad requests are marked ephemeral so they don't allocate persistent KV entries.
zara: implementation note: pad pool must be LIFO to avoid starving medium requests. and we need a bound so it never consumes more than X% headroom.
oliver: agreed. prototype config: pad_limit_fraction=0.07, pad_token_cap=32, pad_eviction=LIFO.
noah: aside: we should detect fragmentation dynamically. propose metric: fragmentation_index = 1 - (sum(allocatable_slots_capacity) / total_slot_capacity) per lane. high index -> many unusable gaps.
grace: nice. we can alert when fragmentation_index > 0.25 for 2m. what action? auto-compact?\zolivia: auto-compact would merge contiguous free gaps into new slot assignments and signal the allocator. risky if inflight KV affinity exists.
oliver: safer approach: schedule compaction window only when inflight_long_count < threshold and no active streaming. compaction should only affect new allocations.
noah: add smoothing to slot-sizing: maintain p75 and p95 histograms per tenant, pick slot = max(min_slot, smooth(p95, alpha=0.15)). and only allow changes every 30s.\zara: that reduces oscillation. also bind slot changes to admission credits so a tenant expanding its slot consumes extra credits immediately; prevents sudden headroom hogging.
grace: what about lane-profiles? small/medium/large lanes with fixed headroom quotas. advantage: predictable packing. downside: fragmentation across lanes if tenants misclassify.
oliver: hybrid: lanes + elastic overflow. primary lane used based on profile, overflow goes to shared lane with lower priority. overflow throttles via credit bucket.
noah: eviction semantics: immediate eviction kills tail. propose "drip-evict": mark victim, allow up to M tokens emission or T ms, then evict. configurable per-tier.
zara: tie "drip-evict" to SLA level: enterprise customers get graceful, free-tier gets aggressive. need billing tags for the extra token cost.\ograce: ops-bot: can we get a staging run of pad-pool + drip-evict?
ops-bot: deploy: patch pad-pool + drip-evict enabled on staging cluster group alpha. smoke tests ok.
oliver: quick query to watch fragmentation_index & pad usage:
```
avg by(lane) (1 - (sum(batcher_allocatable_capacity_bytes{env="staging"}) / sum(batcher_total_capacity_bytes{env="staging"})))
```
and pad usage: `rate(batcher_pad_allocated_count[1m]) / sum(rate(batcher_allocated_slots_total[1m]))`
noah: add metric: avg_compaction_duration and compaction_failed_count.
zara: plan: 1) run staging canary 6h, collect p50/p95/p99 and cost change, 2) if p99 improves and cost delta <5%, roll to canary in prod 5% traffic, 3) monitor fragmentation and kv_miss_rate.\ograce: i'll add dashboard tiles and alert rule.
oliver: follow-ups: implement pad per-GPU soft cap, add credit deduction on slot-size change, and spec compaction gating rules. i'll open PRs.
ops-bot: link: https://staging.console.redwood.ai/d/slotworkbench/frag-pad-5599998888
zara: thanks all. closing thread; track in runtime sprint board. :rocket:
